page.title: Release readiness
page.purpose: Walk the owner through Apple's path — the most opaque part of shipping an iOS app — naming at every rung what is done, what is blocked, and what only a person can do.

priorities.statement: Rungs are ordered, and a later rung never reports ready while an earlier one is not.
priorities.notes: Certificates cannot be ready while enrollment is not. Order is the information.

priorities.statement: Each rung states plainly whether the ramp can complete it or only the owner can.
priorities.notes: Enrollment, identity verification, 2FA, and payment are irreducibly human. Implying automation that cannot exist wastes the owner's time.

priorities.statement: The enrollment rung shows its recurring cost, not just a status.
priorities.notes: $99/yr is a decision. A rung that reads only 'not started' hides that it is a purchase.

priorities.statement: The build-host rung reports both whether it can validate and whether it can produce submittable builds.
priorities.notes: These diverge on an Intel host, and the divergence is dated and foreseeable rather than a surprise.

priorities.statement: Rung state is re-probed, never read from a stored flag.
priorities.notes: A lapsed membership must not continue to read as satisfied.

elements.name: Readiness rungs
elements.description: The ordered ladder from no account to App Review submission. Array order is the dependency order.

elements.name: Rung state
elements.description: The probed state of one rung, carrying a text label as well as a status colour.

elements.name: Completed by
elements.description: Whether the ramp can complete this rung or only the owner can.

elements.name: Cost
elements.description: The monetary cost of a rung where one exists, shown as part of the rung rather than in documentation.

elements.name: Next action
elements.description: The single action that advances the first unsatisfied rung.

elements.name: Deadline
elements.description: The dated external obligation attached to a rung, where one exists.

elements.name: Path without enrollment
elements.description: Statement that a physical-device path exists that requires no enrollment, together with its non-promotable caveat.

states.description: Rung states are being probed; none are asserted yet.
No Apple account has been configured at all, so no rung can even be probed. Distinct from a probed-and-unsatisfied ladder.
Some rungs were probed and others could not be reached; the unprobed ones are explicitly unknown rather than assumed unsatisfied.
Rung state is from an old probe. Age is shown, because a lapsed membership must not continue to read as satisfied.
The readiness probe failed. Reported as a failure rather than as an unsatisfied ladder.
No Apple Developer Program enrollment. The first rung is the only actionable one; every later rung is explicitly blocked by it. The mirror path is surfaced as the one thing that works without it.
Enrollment submitted but not granted. Distinguishes 'waiting on Apple' from 'waiting on you'.
Every rung satisfied, but the fulfilling build host will stop producing submittable builds when the SDK floor next rises. Shown as a dated warning, not a failure.
Every rung satisfied; TestFlight upload is available.

claims.statement: The ladder is presented in dependency order, so the first unsatisfied rung is the first one an owner reads.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-009. Order is the information. A ladder whose rungs can be read in any order is just a checklist.

claims.statement: Every rung shows its state and whether the ramp or the owner completes it.
claims.rationale: The purpose of the surface is to tell the owner what to do next; conflating 'blocked on you' with 'blocked on the system' defeats it.

claims.statement: A rung that costs money displays that cost.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-009. $99/yr is a decision, not a task. A rung that reads only 'not started' hides that it is a purchase.

claims.statement: An unstarted ladder presents the single next action that advances it.
claims.rationale: The ladder exists to answer 'what do I do now'. Showing six blocked rungs without one action does not answer it.

claims.statement: When enrollment is absent, the surface names the physical-device path that needs no enrollment.
claims.rationale: S2I-P1-002. Without this the owner concludes that no physical-device work is possible at all, which is false.

claims.statement: A build host approaching its submittable-build limit shows the dated requirement it will fail.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-004. 'This host may stop working' is not actionable; 'Xcode 27 requires Apple Silicon' is.

claims.statement: A ladder awaiting an Apple decision renders distinguishably from one awaiting an owner action.
claims.rationale: Enrollment review can take days. An owner who cannot tell these apart will either wait on themselves or re-submit something already pending.

claims.statement: Rung state shown to the owner reflects a probe rather than a stored completion flag, so a lapsed or revoked membership stops reading as satisfied.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-009. This is a data-provenance property that cannot be observed from the rendered tree alone; it needs a human or an integration test to attest.

claims.statement: Wherever the no-enrollment physical path is offered, its non-promotable status is stated with it.
claims.rationale: S2I-P1-002. Surfacing the escape hatch without the caveat is misleading in the opposite direction from hiding it.
